records.reason: m200 at 1/1, 50 ul supplies the lower-loading contrast to measured 100 ul and selected 150 ul, testing whether its newly exposed nitro-alcohol response has endpoint-specific loading effects.
m200 at 1/1, 150 ul completes the loading bracket while retaining DCM 600 ul. Its measured pure-EA 100/150 ul agreement provides context, without establishing invariance at 1/1.
m200 at 2/1, 50 ul extends the selected low-loading curve and contrasts with measured 100 ul where both endpoints rose strongly relative to 1/1.
m200 at 2/1, 150 ul completes a two-ratio, three-loading comparison with observed anchors, distinguishing loading invariance from ratio-dependent onset or completion shifts.
m204 at 5/1, 150 ul directly contrasts with measured 100 ul and anchors the selected higher-loading ratio pair in a primary alcohol distinct from m200 and m61.
m204 at 10/1, 150 ul tests loading transfer of its steep measured 100 ul response and whether the large 5/1-to-10/1 increment persists at increased loading.
m75 at 2/1, 100 ul fills the loading interval between measured 50/150 ul, where onset differs by 7.81 ml and the 50 ul elution interval is exceptionally short.
m75 at 10/1, 100 ul supplies the second missing loading midpoint. Together the two points test whether onset interpolation and completion loading effects change with ratio.
Salicylaldehyde m197 at 1/1, 100 ul anchors a controlled hydroxyaldehyde curve beyond the mapped brominated analogues, retaining its PE loading solvent.
m197 at 5/1, 100 ul tests the unmeasured lower-ratio completion shape. Its predicted decline from 1/1 remains a competing model response, not measured evidence.
m197 at 10/1, 100 ul distinguishes continued shallow onset from joint growth and connects the selected lower-ratio points to the selected 20/1 loading bridge.
m197 at 20/1, 100 ul completes the fixed-loading curve and interpolates measured 50/150 ul anchors, avoiding a loading-confounded interpretation of its ratio slope.
Benzyl acrylate m22 at 2/1, 150 ul supplies a matched lower-ratio anchor before measured 5/1, testing ester transfer after m15/m16 proved shallow and m21 completion plateaued.
m22 at 20/1, 150 ul connects measured 5/1 and 50/1 under identical loading, locating growth across an ordinary ester environment without importing the m20 ether-acrylate slope.
Trifluoroethyl acrylate m17 at 1/1, 150 ul establishes a fixed-loading baseline for its measured 10/1 point, extending ester coverage to a fluorinated alkoxy environment.
m17 at 20/1, 150 ul completes a controlled sequence through measured 10/1. Its DCM loading remains explicit when comparing with PE-loaded hydrophobic acrylates.
Para-methylacetophenone m32 at 2/1, 150 ul anchors a same-loading curve before its measured 5/1 completion elevation, improving ordinary ketone response coverage.
m32 at 10/1, 150 ul tests whether its early measured 5/1 onset persists while completion grows, or both endpoints rise as currently predicted.
Meta-methylacetophenone m41 at 2/1, 150 ul supplies a lower-ratio anchor for its measured 10/1 response, complementing the selected para-isomer curve.
m41 at 5/1, 150 ul locates its intermediate progression toward measured 10/1. PE versus DCM loading prevents attributing differences from m32 solely to methyl position.
Dimethylpyridine m141 at 1/1, 100 ul contrasts with measured 150 ul and anchors a new fixed-100 ul curve after onset and completion showed different historical residual signs.
m141 at 2/1, 100 ul adds a second matched loading contrast against measured 150 ul, separating a loading-associated offset from its lower-ratio slope.
m141 at 5/1, 100 ul extends the selected fixed-loading sequence into the intermediate basic-nitrogen regime. Its measured 10/1 point uses 150 ul and remains contextual.
Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde m198 at 1/1, 150 ul extends its measured pure-EA baseline, testing transfer from differentiated para-nitro aldehyde and ketone curves.
m198 at 10/1, 150 ul measures onset and completion growth under the same injection conditions, testing whether nitro placement limits transfer of the steep m193 response.
m198 at 20/1, 150 ul supplies the controlled continuation of selected 10/1, distinguishing sustained joint growth from completion-dominated or shallower behavior.
Dibenzyl ether m213 at 2/1, 100 ul connects its measured pure-EA and 20/1 anchors, testing a noncarbonyl ether response outside the recently investigated polar tails.
m213 at 5/1, 100 ul tests its predicted intermediate completion elevation through a controlled curve. The related dibenzylamine response provides context without establishing an ether correction.
Methoxybenzoate m87 at 2/1, 150 ul establishes a matched lower-ratio anchor for its measured 10/1 and 50/1 curve, testing ether/ester transfer in a ring-conjugated environment.
m87 at 5/1, 150 ul locates intermediate growth before measured 10/1, distinguishing its response from shallow hydrophobic acrylates and the plateauing phenoxyethyl acrylate.
Chlorinated aryl ketone m169 at 2/1, 100 ul extends its measured 1/1 anchor, adding a controlled carbonyl environment with a longer aliphatic substituent.
m169 at 10/1, 100 ul completes the same-loading extension, testing whether its onset and completion slopes resemble nearby ordinary aryl ketones or differ with carbonyl environment.

hypotheses.content: Alcohol response is conditional on molecular environment, ratio, loading and endpoint. m200 and m204 grow strongly in both endpoints, whereas m61 has an inverse onset response whose magnitude changes with loading. Their loading responses cannot be inferred from a shared alcohol correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m200 factorial and m204 ratio pair can distinguish ratio-dependent loading effects from useful local loading invariance, improving separate onset and completion predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m200 loading effects differ between 1/1 and 2/1, and does m204 retain its steep 5/1-to-10/1 rise at 150 ul?

hypotheses.content: Phenylmalonate m75 has ratio-dependent endpoint loading associations. Increasing loading from 50 to 150 ul advances onset at both measured ratios, while completion decreases at 2/1 and increases slightly at 10/1. The very short 2/1, 50 ul interval remains unreplicated.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two missing 100 ul measurements constrain onset interpolation and completion interactions without assuming a global carbonyl loading law or smooth interpolation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At each ratio, does 100 ul interpolate the measured endpoints or reveal additional conditional structure?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyaldehyde transfer remains conditional. m186 retains nearly fixed onset while completion grows. The m197 20/1 loading anchors do not establish its lower-ratio curve, and the isolated m117 near-reversal limits reliable transfer from that input.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A controlled salicylaldehyde curve can distinguish completion shoulders from joint growth across donor/carbonyl environments without propagating an exceptional label as a deterministic response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m197 show a lower-ratio completion decrease, sustained growth, or a plateau, and is its 20/1 loading midpoint coherent with the measured bracket?

hypotheses.content: Ester response depends on substituent and carbonyl environment. m15 and m16 remain shallow across 1/1-to-10/1, m21 completion is nearly flat from 2/1 to 5/1, and m20 grows strongly. These observations do not fix benzyl-acrylate, fluorinated-acrylate or methoxybenzoate slopes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected ester curves teach structural limits of shallow and steep response transfer across ordinary Row chemistry.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m22, m17 and m87 develop onset and completion growth under their own fixed injection conditions?

hypotheses.content: Nitro position and carbonyl environment may change ratio sensitivity. Measured para-nitro carbonyl curves and the ortho-nitroaldehyde m198 pure-EA baseline do not establish a shared response through PE enrichment.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The fixed-loading m198 sequence tests transfer among structures with similar broad polarity descriptors while allowing distinct onset and completion slopes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m198 grow jointly from 1/1 through 20/1, or depart from the steep para-nitroaldehyde response?

hypotheses.content: Ordinary aryl-ketone response shapes remain incompletely determined by their sparse anchors. Methyl substitution and aliphatic carbonyl substituents may change endpoint slopes; cross-molecule injection differences remain explicit.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected m32, m41 and m169 curves broaden ordinary condition-response coverage and distinguish molecular offsets from endpoint-specific ratio sensitivity.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m32 retain early onset beyond 5/1, how does m41 approach its measured 10/1 endpoints, and where does m169 begin growing?

feedback_interpretation: The authoritative state is 749 observed records and 2,581 candidates; embedded 717/2,613 summaries are stale. H18 is revised: m194 at 150 ul has completion 24.99/27.33/28.18 ml across 0/1, 1/1 and 2/1, rejecting transfer of the 100 ul 1/1-to-2/1 decline to 150 ul. Its early onset and long pure-EA completion reinforce endpoint-specific loading associations. m21 completion changes only 11.92-to-11.93 ml from 2/1 to 5/1, weakening transfer of m20's strong growth. H13 gains support as conditional heterogeneity: the new m61 150 ul anchor places an onset decrease of 9.13 ml between 2/1 and 5/1, while completion decreases only 2.40 ml. m200 and m204 instead grow strongly in both endpoints, motivating controlled loading tests rather than a shared alcohol correction. H15 is narrowed: m25 at 150 ul increases from 11.38/24.23 to 16.94/39.22 ml between 10/1 and 20/1, less than historically forecast; its 50/1 anchor uses 100 ul. The m75 loading comparison reveals a much larger onset than completion effect and different completion directions across ratios. H17's immediate lactone question is answered by joint growth already present at m181 5/1, 50 ul, measuring 11.46/18.46 ml. H26 gains completion-dominated evidence from m186, whose onset stays near 4.6 ml through 10/1. The m117 10/1 record has V2-V1 approximately -0.075 ml; this isolated label-coherence issue remains flagged with its supplied values unchanged and does not establish a reproducible peak or mechanism. It is distinct from the rejected original m13/m80 prediction-anomaly premise. H27 is supported by shallow m15/m16 responses. The m72 and boronate extensions also reduce their immediate curve gaps. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over measured ranges; m177, m120 and m207 repeatability remains unresolved. All residuals discussed are historical premeasurement errors, and candidate values remain predictions only.
batch_rationale: Recent feedback answers several previous questions and shifts acquisition toward specific interactions and less sampled structural curves. The m200 measurements form a controlled loading comparison across a steep ratio increment; m204 tests transfer of another strong alcohol response. The two m75 midpoints address a substantial onset association with different completion behavior across ratios. m197 and m198 extend hydroxy- and nitroaldehyde transfer without treating m117's exceptional record as a reliable response template. Ester, ordinary ketone, pyridine and dibenzyl-ether sequences supply molecular offsets and ratio slopes outside the repeatedly investigated exceptional surfaces. No further allocation is assigned to the now-measured adviser nominations or routine completion of established grids.

Their loading responses cannot be inferred from a shared alcohol correction.

hypotheses.content: Phenylmalonate m75 has ratio-dependent endpoint loading associations. Increasing loading from 50 to 150 ul advances onset at both measured ratios, while completion decreases at 2/1 and increases slightly at 10/1. The very short 2/1, 50 ul interval remains unreplicated.

hypotheses.content: Ester response depends on substituent and carbonyl environment. m15 and m16 remain shallow across 1/1-to-10/1, m21 completion is nearly flat from 2/1 to 5/1, and m20 grows strongly. These observations do not fix benzyl-acrylate, fluorinated-acrylate or methoxybenzoate slopes.

hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m22, m17 and m87 develop onset and completion growth under their own fixed injection conditions?

hypotheses.content: Nitro position and carbonyl environment may change ratio sensitivity. Measured para-nitro carbonyl curves and the ortho-nitroaldehyde m198 pure-EA baseline do not establish a shared response through PE enrichment.

hypotheses.content: Ordinary aryl-ketone response shapes remain incompletely determined by their sparse anchors. Methyl substitution and aliphatic carbonyl substituents may change endpoint slopes; cross-molecule injection differences remain explicit.

The m117 10/1 record has V2-V1 approximately -0.075 ml; this isolated label-coherence issue remains flagged with its supplied values unchanged and does not establish a reproducible peak or mechanism. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over measured ranges; m177, m120 and m207 repeatability remains unresolved.
